title: Strong diamond property for elementary hammock reductions
statement: Let $P$ be a small ordinary category, let $T\subseteq P$ be a wide subcategory containing identities and closed under composition, let $x,y\in P$, and let $q\geq0$. Use the fixed-word diagrams of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus], with only the letters $+,-$. An unreduced hammock is a finite commutative rectangular diagram with $q+1$ rows from $x$ to $y$, all vertical arrows pointing down and lying in $T$, identity vertical arrows at the endpoints, a uniform horizontal direction in each column, and all leftward arrows in $T$. A length-zero diagram exists precisely when $x=y$ and has only identity vertical arrows. No alternation or nonidentity condition is imposed. Define $D\rightsquigarrow D'$ to mean one of the following operations on such diagrams: delete one column all of whose horizontal arrows are identities, identifying its two equal vertex columns and retaining their vertical arrows; or replace two adjacent columns of the same direction by their rowwise composites, deleting the intervening vertex column and retaining all other vertical arrows. These operations produce unreduced hammocks with the same $P,T,x,y,q$. If $D\rightsquigarrow D_1$ and $D\rightsquigarrow D_2$, then either $D_1=D_2$, or there is an unreduced hammock $E$ with $D_1\rightsquigarrow E$ and $D_2\rightsquigarrow E$. Equality here includes the signed word, all vertex objects, and all horizontal and vertical arrows.
